title: Separatedness of an admissible finite scheme quotient
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, let $M\to S$ be a separated morphism of finite type, and let a finite group $G$ act by $S$-automorphisms on $M$. Suppose the action is admissible, meaning every orbit lies in an affine open, and that $q:M\to Q$ is an admissible finite scheme quotient [def-per-admissible-finite-scheme-quotient]. Thus $q$ is finite surjective, its point fibres are the orbits, and $\mathcal O_Q=(q_*\mathcal O_M)^G$. Then the induced morphism $Q\to S$ is separated. No freeness assumption and no invertibility assumption on $|G|$ is imposed.

source.place: Exposé IX §1.4, printed pp.132--133, finite admissible quotient construction. This is the separatedness property of that construction; the additional conclusion is not asserted in lem-per-admissible-quotient-generic-degree. The arbitrary-action statement is used, not the free-action quotient of Stacks Tags 02Z4 or 0BBM.

proof.text: Write $p:M\to S$ for the given structure morphism and $h:Q\to S$ for the induced structure morphism; thus $h\circ q=p$. By the quotient hypothesis [def-per-admissible-finite-scheme-quotient], $q$ is finite. Its underlying map is a topological quotient map and in particular surjective; this is precisely surjectivity of a scheme morphism [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Consequently $q$ is a surjective morphism over $S$.

source.place: Expose IX 1.4, printed pp.132--133: finite admissible quotients; structure maps to the original base.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper] to the finite morphism $q:M\to Q$. It follows that $q$ is proper. By the definition of proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], $q$ is universally closed. This application needs no hypothesis that $Q$ or $M$ is proper over $S$.

source.place: Stacks Tag 01WN, lemma-finite-proper: finite implies affine and proper; Tag 01W1, definition-proper.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-universally-closed-separated] with its $X=M$, $Y=Q$, $f=q$, and its two structure morphisms $p$ and $h$. The relation $h\circ q=p$ and surjectivity were checked in Step 1, universal closedness in Step 2, and $p$ is separated by hypothesis. The cited result therefore makes $h:Q\to S$ separated, as required. Its hypotheses make no reference to freeness of the action or invertibility of $|G|$, so neither is required.
